aspects.says: int's range is asymmetric, so Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is negative and Math.abs(hash) % n can be a negative index; Math.floorMod takes the divisor's sign.
basis: section:Integer Arithmetic Wraps Without an Error, Even When the Result Goes Into a long

aspects.says: A double holds a binary fraction, so computed values are compared with a tolerance, not ==.
basis: section:A double Holds a Binary Fraction, So Compare Computed Values With a Tolerance That Fits Their Size

aspects.says: Math.multiplyExact and Math.addExact throw ArithmeticException where plain arithmetic would wrap.
basis: section:Integer Arithmetic Wraps Without an Error, Even When the Result Goes Into a long
aspects.reason: a test sees only the number a method returns, so it can't tell an exact-arithmetic call from correct widening; the tenant-storage practice accepts either

aspects.says: Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException, while the same division in floating point returns a value.
basis: section:Integer Division by Zero Throws; Floating-Point Division Returns Infinity or NaN, and NaN Equals Nothing

aspects.says: Floating-point division by zero returns Infinity or NaN, and every comparison with NaN is false, so !(x > limit) is not x <= limit.
basis: section:Integer Division by Zero Throws; Floating-Point Division Returns Infinity or NaN, and NaN Equals Nothing

aspects.says: A fixed tolerance fails as values grow, because doubles are spaced by their size; near 1e9 a tolerance of 1e-9 acts like ==.
basis: section:A double Holds a Binary Fraction, So Compare Computed Values With a Tolerance That Fits Their Size

aspects.says: Unboxing a null wrapper throws NullPointerException, as when an absent Map value is assigned to an int.
basis: section:A Wrapper Is an Object: It Can Be null, and == Compares References

aspects.says: == on two wrappers compares references; Integer.valueOf is only guaranteed to cache -128 to 127, so equal larger values compare false.
basis: section:A Wrapper Is an Object: It Can Be null, and == Compares References

aspects.says: Integer arithmetic is done in the operands' type and wraps without an error, even when the result is assigned to a long; a long operand widens only the operations after it.
basis: section:Integer Arithmetic Wraps Without an Error, Even When the Result Goes Into a long
